articleTitle: Augmented Reality Indoor Navigation with Smart Appliance control
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: This proposed work explores the application of augmented reality (AR) for indoor navigation in emergency situations and large spaces using Unity NavMesh and the A* algorithm. It provides real-time information about college class-rooms and enhances accessibility for people with disabilities. The proposed system utilizes Vuforia and Unity to construct the AR environment, integrating QR code scanning using the ZXING SDK, as well as the smart control of light bulbs, fans, and other appliances through ESP32, relay modules, and the Blynk API. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in improving navigation accuracy and accessibility for users. Furthermore, the system’s real-time updates, user-friendly interface, and remote appliance control offer a versatile solution for various indoor environments. The proposed work presents a detailed explanation of the literature review, the operating architecture, discusses its social impact, limitations, and future scope, highlighting its potential to revolutionize indoor navigation and accessibility for all.

articleTitle: A Novel State-Feedback Controller for Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machines
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: This paper presents a state feedback controller for speed control for permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) drives. Both surface and interior PMSMs (i.e., SPMSM and IPMSM) have been considered. The state feedback gain in the proposed method is tuned based on the pole placement method, where the locations of the system poles are selected with respect to the desired control bandwidth. The proposed control method achieves the decoupling of q- and d- axes currents without linearization in the entire speed range. The performance of the proposed control method for load-torque rejection is compared against two widely used PI-based control methods, i.e., active damping and 2-degree-of-freedom techniques. It is verified that the proposed state-feedback control method achieves superior performance (e.g., reduced over/under-shoot in transients) for control of PMSMs compared to the PI-based methods.

articleTitle: Modeling of Textile Antenna Sensors for Breast Cancer Detection Using Artificial Intelligence Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: This paper proposes modelling and simulations for textile antenna-based sensors acting as tumor detection system for breast using artificial intelligence. The proposed textile sensors are lightweight, comfortable to wear with low fabrication cost at microwave frequencies. The sensors are modelled with a 3-layer breast phantom with skin, gland, and fatty tissue, along with a tumor with high water content. Simulations are conducted using three dimensions electromagnetic wave CST Studio simulator with 4 elements of antenna-based sensors. The utilized sensor operates on breast phantom in the band from 3.5 to 5 GHz with an average gain of 6 dBi. Tumors are simulated with diameters from 5 mm to 15 mm at the centre of breast and 45<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup> offset of the centre. For tumor detection, different machine learning techniques are applied to classify between malignant and benign cells using Scattering parameters. These techniques provide accurate estimation for tumor detection at different tumor sizes. 98% classification accuracy is realized for centre and shifted tumor using developed machine learning techniques.

articleTitle: Low Power and High Speed Comparator Design in Quantum-dot Cellular Automata
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Quantum-dot Cellular Automata is a novel nanocomputing technology that allows the designing of extraordinarily low-power and highly dense circuits with very high operating frequencies. Digital comparators are utilized in many devices, including Central Processing Units, microcontrollers, servo motors and process controllers, to address data comparisons and other arithmetic operations. This work presents an energy-efficient and high-speed optimized QCA comparator design. The proposed comparator design utilizes two XOR gates with parallel input feed and two majority gates. The proposed design achieves considerable improvements in total energy dissipation, QCA cell count and latency compared to the preliminary designs. The results are also compared based on the Efficient Complexity Function, area usage and certain other metrics.

articleTitle: Spatially-Resolved Hyperlocal Weather Prediction and Anomaly Detection Using IoT Sensor Networks and Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Accurate and timely hyperlocal weather predictions are essential for various applications, ranging from agriculture to disaster management. In this paper, we propose a novel approach that combines hyperlocal weather prediction and anomaly detection using IoT sensor networks and advanced machine learning techniques. Our approach leverages data from multiple spatially-distributed yet relatively close locations and IoT sensors to create high-resolution weather models capable of predicting short-term, localized weather conditions such as temperature, pressure, and humidity. By monitoring changes in weather parameters across these locations, our system is able to enhance the spatial resolution of predictions and effectively detect anomalies in real-time. Additionally, our system employs unsupervised learning algorithms to identify unusual weather patterns, providing timely alerts. Our findings indicate that this system has the potential to enhance decision-making.Hyperlocal weather prediction, Anomaly detection, IoT sensor networks, Machine learning, Spatial resolution, Weather monitoring

articleTitle: Versioning of SysML v2 for simulation by using Graph Databases in a CI/CD process
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: The new systems modeling language SysML v2 brings many changes for requirement engineering. With its constructs to address the specific needs of systems engineering it will be the new standard in its field. Currently there is barely any (free) software available to work with it. We set up an ADAS-simulation and used the SysML v2 to define parameters of the simulation. To read SysML v2 we developed a parser to map the code into Python-compatible JSON. Using this parser the specifications are read, the simulation set up and KPIs in the SysML v2 are rewritten according to simulation result. With a graph-versioning system searchability and persistence are guaranteed. SysML v2 is closer to programming languages than XML. With the current standard of SysML every vendor of external tools brought their own standard. Anyone who has worked with SysML knows the struggle incompatibility. In this work the proper SysML 2 standard was mapped into a database compatible form and versioning applied.

articleTitle: An Investigation of Context-Aware Object Detection based on Scene Recognition
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Visual scene understanding for humans entails identifying regions of interest and then reasoning about information gained through their contextual analysis. Attempts to reproduce this process using Computer Vision techniques play an important role in improving the performance of Object Detection and general scene understanding algorithms. In this paper, we augment the training algorithm of an Object Detection model by integrating contextual information in the form of ‘scene labels’, through various methods to identify the superior approach. Several deep learning models were implemented and evaluated; results show that the Contextually Aware Object Detection Model performed the best, producing the highest classification accuracy of 75.14% and mean bounding box IoU of 0.69 on the constructed dataset. This was achieved by virtue of an auxiliary scene classification model used to make image scene predictions during the training phase.

articleTitle: Single CFOA-based Grounded Negative Impedance Simulator Circuit
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: This paper presents a novel grounded negative series RL and RC simulator circuit. The presented circuit uses one current feedback operational amplifier (CFOA) and three passive elements without requiring any matching condition. The proposed circuit can also be configured as negative capacitance in series with frequency dependent positive resistor (FDPR) and negative capacitance divider with proper selection of passive elements. Various analyses, including frequency, transient, and temperature analysis have been performed to support the theoretical findings using macro-model of CFOA AD844 with PSPICE. To check the workability of the proposed negative series RL and negative series RC circuits, inductance cancellation circuit and capacitance cancellation circuit are given as application examples.

articleTitle: LoRaWAN: A Boon for the Remote Region IoT Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: IoT has paved the way for enhancing and transforming the quality of life through remote automation and monitoring via various short-range, long-range, and cellular network connectivity technologies. These technologies are very efficient in urban regions but struggle in remote geographically challenging environments hence stopping the implementation of IoT devices in such regions. In such a scenario, LoRaWAN emerges as a revolutionary technology, providing efficient connectivity and reliable communication for remote region IoT application devices. This paper aims to provide valuable insights into the network architecture capabilities of LoRaWAN for remote region IoT applications.

articleTitle: Automated Lung Cancer Detection Using Lightweight Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Due to growing lung cancer rates and COVID19 pandemic awareness, automated lung cancer diagnosis has garnered focus in recent years. In medical image processing, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have shown promise for accurate and efficient lung cancer identification. This research proposes the use of a lightweight CNN architecture to identify lung cancer. The lightweight CNN balances model complexity with performance, making it suited for deployment on mobile devices and edge computing systems. The proposed technique is tested using a heterogeneous lung cancer dataset with chest X-ray pictures. During training, our lightweight CNN achieved 99% dataset accuracy, superseding other models in comparison. The model's sensitivity and specificity, critical in lung cancer screening, reduces false negatives and positives. Precision and automated lung cancer detection may speed up early identification and care, improving patient outcomes. CNN's lightweight architecture allows real-time inference on resource-constrained devices, expanding lung cancer screening in rural and underprivileged areas. In conclusion, a lightweight convolutional neural network can identify lung cancer automatically. This approach's 99% validation accuracy on a difficult lung cancer dataset shows it’s potential to help doctors make accurate diagnoses leading to aids in timely lung cancer detection and improved health outcomes.

articleTitle: Single CMOS VCII Based Inverse Filter Configuration
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Inverse filters are frequently employed in various areas of signal processing, control systems, instrumentation, and communication to recover a distorted signal. This paper presents a generalized structure of a second generation voltage conveyor (VCII)-based voltage-mode (VM) multifunction inverse filter structure employing one VCII- and three admittances. The proposed structure can realize, inverse low pass filter (ILPF), inverse high pass filter (IHPF), and inverse band pass filter (IBPF) from the same circuit configuration by choosing appropriate combination of the different admittances. PSPICE simulations employing 180nm TSMC CMOS technology characteristics are used to validate the applicability of the suggested filter functions. śThe sensitivity, monte-carlo, temperature, and output noise analyses are carried out to test the effectiveness of the proposed inverse filter structure.

articleTitle: Unsupervised Segmentation and Data Augmentation in Image Sequences of Skeletal Muscle Contraction by Cycle-Consistent Generative Adversarial Network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: This paper investigates a method addressing the unsupervised segmentation and joint data augmentation in medical ultrasound imaging based on the modified CycleGAN. Accurate quantification of fascia and muscle is the key for the diagnostics of neuromuscular disorders based on the analysis of image sequences of skeletal muscle contraction. Although the Deep Learning (DL) models represent encouraging results, some challenges exist. The traditional models don’t consider the complex interaction between tissues within a muscle and its surroundings, which reduces the performance of the fascia segmentation. Also, the DL requires many annotated datasets, which ignores dealing with noisy and complex ultrasound images. To overcome these issues, we propose a method to generate realistic images, and then present an unsupervised fascia segmentation method. The results show that our method improves the segmentation accuracy in noisy and complex ultrasound images compared to the traditional methods.

articleTitle: Experimental Investigations towards the Design of Power Management System Using Indoor Photovoltaic
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: With the increasing popularity of Internet-of-Things (IoT) based building automation and lighting controls in the interior, the power management of IoT devices is a concern. Researchers globally are working on Indoor high-performance photovoltaics, which can power IoT devices. Here arises the need for experimentation with Indoor Photovoltaics (IPV) under varying interior lighting conditions that includes both artificial light and daylight. This paper focuses on experimental verification of the IPV characterization under indoor lighting conditions, adopting the recent human-centric lighting challenges. The paper presents empirical modeling of indoor irradiance and Photovoltaic cells to estimate its I-V characteristics and focuses on their operation at indoor illumination levels. A crucial requirement for accomplishing self-sustainability is the ability of IoT devices to be self-powered.

articleTitle: High-Isolation, Wideband Two-Element MIMO Antenna with Novel Decoupling Coupling Structure for Millimeter Wave 5G Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: The article presents a compact, novel, inverted Pshaped antenna operating at Ka-band. The antenna is designed to resonate at frequency f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> = 30 GHz. The single-element antenna is expanded to a two-element MIMO. Various antenna orientation arrangements are studied to comprehend the effect of mutual coupling. Out-of-these mirrored antenna elements facing outward have resulted in better isolation of 22.95 dB with a bandwidth of 27.30-34.83 GHz. However, a slight mismatch in reflection coefficients is observed due to minor surface wave coupling. Further, a novel decoupling structure with a combination of inverted H- and T-shaped is engraved in the ground plane to enhance the isolation and antenna performance. The overall MIMO antenna profile is 1.3λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> x 0.52λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>. It resulted in a maximum isolation of 35.17 dB with a bandwidth of 26.3633.64 GHz. The maximum achieved gain is 3.2 dB. The proposed antenna is validated with diversity performance and is suitable for 5G wireless applications.

articleTitle: Two Layer Security for Confidentiality in User Assisted Cooperative Noma System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: User-Assisted Cooperative Non-orthogonal multiple access (UA-CNOMA) is a promising radio access technique for 5G networks allowing multiple users to share the same time-frequency resource. However, as the number of connected users continues to grow, ensuring data security has become a critical concern. This paper proposes a two-layer security scheme based on Physical Layer Security (PLS) and chaotic encryption to enhance the confidentiality of user data transmission in UA-CNOMA systems. The proposed system incorporates a user-assisted relay and employs chaotic encryption with a logistic map at the transmitter. To further enhance security, the control values of the logistic map are encrypted using PLS. The performance of the proposed scheme is evaluated to demonstrate its superiority over traditional PLS-based NOMA systems. It is inferred from the simulation that the proposed scheme provides enhanced confidentiality in data transmission than the existing techniques.

articleTitle: A Modified Circular Shaped Flexible UWB Antenna for Wireless Body Area Network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: A conformal ultrawideband antenna of 25 × 25 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> is proposed in this paper for wearable applications. A flexible polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) substrate of thickness 1.4 mm is used to design this structure. The antenna consists of a modified elliptical geometry as the radiating part and a partial ground plane. To obtain wider bandwidth, two rectangular shape slots are etched in the ground surface. The antenna operates from 3.81-11.69 GHz with a peak gain of 8.2 dBi at 9.9 GHz. The proposed design shows good compatibility and impedance matching when bent along x and y axis. To study the effect of antenna’s radiation on human tissue Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) is analyzed. The SAR at 4.5 GHz are 0.785 and 0.308 W/kg for 1g and 10 g of tissue, respectively. The proposed antenna is suitable for Wireless Body Area Network (WBAN), wearable and IoT application.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Powered Multiclass Classification of DDoS Attacks on 6G-Connected IoT Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: The rapid expansion of the 6G network and the widespread deployment of IoT devices resulted in challenging the effective detection and mitigation of distributed denial of service (DDoS) attacks originating from Internet of Things (IoT) sources. This paper presents an approach to handle this difficulty using machine learning and deep learning models. The approach uses Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Random Forest classifiers for binary classification, and Artificial Neural Network (ANN) model for determining the precise type of attack among nine classes. Fisher's Score and Recursive Feature Elimination with Cross Validation (RFECV) feature selection techniques are employed in the proposed approach for increasing the effectiveness of the system. The proposed approach is validated on the Canadian Institute for Cybersecurity-2019 dataset and the model achieves an accuracy rate of 99.5% for binary classification and more than 90% for different class classification.

Author Keywords: Recursive Feature Elimination with Cross Validation

articleTitle: Enhanced Average-Value Modeling of Voltage-Source Inverters in Variable Frequency Drives for Efficient Simulation of Marine Propulsion Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Variable-frequency drive (VFD) systems utilize voltage-source inverters (VSIs) and are employed extensively in many applications, including marine propulsion. For efficient simulations and studies of such systems, average-value models (AVMs) of VSIs are indispensable. Recently, a so-called directly-interfaced AVM (DI-AVM) has been developed for line-commutated and voltage-source converters. In this paper, the DIAVM is developed for VSIs in the converter reference frame, which has advantages for machine-converter systems. The DI-AVM is implemented in electromagnetic transient (EMT) simulation programs as a resistance/conductance matrix instead of controlled voltage/current sources that are used conventionally. The advantages of the proposed DI-AVM are demonstrated on a ship propulsion system implemented in PSCAD/EMTDC. The proposed DI-AVM offers significant computational advantages compared to the conventional AVMs of VSIs by achieving higher numerical accuracy and allowing larger time step sizes.

articleTitle: Computational Design and Development of On-Board Device for Driver’s Health Monitoring using Microfluidic Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: As more accidents happen, particularly in continuous driving in commercial vehicles, maintaining safety while operating a vehicle on congested highways and roads is becoming increasingly difficult. Continuous driving may impair a driver’s ability to drive safely by reducing their attention span, environmental awareness, situational awareness, and critical decision-making abilities. It’s critical to have a system in place to monitor the health of the driver because the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTS) estimates that each year there are 100,000 police-reported crashes involving drowsy driving and fatigue, which result in close to 800 fatalities and 50,000 injuries. This paper introduces a new, highly advanced driver health and fatigue monitoring system that continuously monitors the health of the driver and displays information onboard. In this paper, we first highlight issues and emerging trends in the research community for fatigue management and health monitoring while driving, and secondly, we also propose a model that consists of a microfluidic chip that senses sweat and measures blood cortisol levels, which is integrated with a signal processing unit and an onboard display unit. This introduces the idea of safety due to fatigue. Conceptually, we designed and simulated the microfluidic sensors in COMSOL Multiphysics and examined the outcomes.

articleTitle: Decomposed and Hybridized Deep Learning Models for an Application to Stock Price Prediction
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Deep learning algorithms like long short term memory and convolutional neural network models are widely used for prediction tasks including stock market data. Decomposition algorithms like empirical mode decomposition and complete ensemble empirical mode decomposition algorithms are used to decompose time series data into different frequency spectra. These methods are used to analyze financial time series data effectively. But due to lack of data pr-eprocessing and mode mixing issues, models based on these methods may not perform well. In this study, three hybridized models: CEEMD-Normalized-CNN-LSTM, VMD-CNN-LSTM and VMD-LSTM are proposed to address the above issues. The proposed hybridized models are validated using four standard stock price datasets. Comparative performance analysis between different hybridized models reveals that the proposed models perform well compared to some of the well-known existing stock price prediction models. The experimental analysis conclude that the proposed VMD-CNN-LSTM outperforms the other existing well known models.

articleTitle: Lithium-Ion Battery Health Prediction Using a GRU Model with Protective Characteristic
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: An innovative battery management system (BMS) is crucial for verifying the credibility and safety of electric vehicles (EVs) and other electrical devices. The precise state of health (SOH) estimation of the Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) holds great importance in a BMS. Battery SOH is often committed by the utilization of suitable data-driven approaches and metrics. This study presents an alternative approach for examining the SOH of batteries through the use of a gated recurrent unit (GRU) as an estimating method. Finally, the Oxford battery datasets is subjected to both training and testing procedures. The validity of the proposed method's adaptability is shown by tests managed to estimate the SOH of a battery cell. The performance of our proposed method is validated on the battery dataset of Oxford, where the average RMSE is 0.31%.Graphical Abstract—

articleTitle: A Time-aware Knowledge Graphs model for Explainable recommendation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: The transparency of knowledge graphs has garnered significant attention in the field of explainable recommendations. Existing works have not taken into account the factor of timeliness in the modeling process, which hinders the accurate learning of user and item representations. To address this research gap, we propose a time-aware recommendation knowledge graph model. By incorporating time embedding into each step of the modeling process, we better model the recommendation paths and improve the effectiveness of recommendations. We conducted experiments on two datasets, demonstrating the superiority of our proposed model.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Lightweight Ciphers for securing images
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: In the digital age, the security of sensitive information and data has become a paramount concern. The modern conventional encryption algorithms are very efficient, but they are very complex and need a lot of resources. This has led to the development and implementation of lightweight ciphers designed specifically for image encryption. Four algorithms namely Present, Lightweight encryption Algorithm (LEA), Twine and Secure IoT(SIT) are implemented to encrypt and decrypt images and their performance is analyzed. The correlation values of the images before encryption is found to be around 0.9 showing strong correlation whereas after encryption it is found to be very less in the range oof 0.0005 which clearly shows the randomization of the pixels and hence good security. The execution times was less than one second for LEA algorithm and hence efficient for multimedia applications.

articleTitle: Pothole Detection using Smartphone: A Driver Assistant
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: India has an extensive road network that becomes degraded over time, causing potholes and other hazardous conditions for drivers. Potholes can cause physical injury and vehicle damage, so their detection is crucial. While some existing systems help drivers identify potholes, they lack precise localization and are location-dependent. In this paper, a cost-effective solution that utilizes mobile phone cameras and a deep neural network (Single Shot MultiBox Detector with MobileNet) for real-time pothole detection and localization is presented. The system alerts drivers about detected potholes instantly and achieved good mean Average Precision. Our solution aims to improve road safety and minimize vehicle damage.

articleTitle: A Q-NF Pairing in NOMA-IoT System Under Im-SIC
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: In this paper, we have proposed a Quadrature Near-Far (Q-NF) pairing scheme and obtained the lower bound conditions for optimizing the power allocation (PA) coefficients in presence of imperfect successive interference cancellation (Im-SIC) for non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) based internet of things (IoTs) system. This paper also discusses the challenges faced during the IoT device pairing and power allocation in multiple NOMA users scenario under minimum rate constraints. Simulation results show that our proposed Q-NF pairing scheme and optimum power allocation coefficient strategy outperform the other user pairing and power allocation strategies in terms of total sum-rate capacity, overall-bit error rate (BER), and outage probability.

articleTitle: TrALPR: Automatic License Plate Recognition using Transformers
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Nowadays, with the increase in population, there is also a massive increase in vehicles on the road, increasing traffic congestion and other traffic-related problems. Because of this, many cities and metropolitan are facing issues while maintaining order on the roads and traffic. Many administrations are looking towards automatic processes that can help to maintain the order on the road. For this problem, Automatic License Plate Recognition (ALPR) models can help in better management of vehicles and transportation. In this paper, the presented Automatic License Plate Recognition system can recognize the License Plate Number from images of vehicles with great accuracy. In the proposed work, a complete end-to-end transformer (encoder-decoder) architecture-based model is developed for Automatic License Plate Recognition.

articleTitle: Self-supervised Language Identification ASR models for Low Resource Indic Languages
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Self-supervised automatic speech recognition (ASR) is a technique that has gained popularity in recent years due to its ability to improve ASR accuracy using large amounts of unlabeled data. Language identification (LID) is another important technique that has been used to identify the language of speech segments, which can be useful for developing ASR models for multilingual environments. This paper presents a novel approach to self-supervised ASR using LID, where the ASR model is pre-trained on large amounts of unlabeled data, and the language of the speech segments is identified during training. The identified language is then used to guide the training of the ASR model, resulting in improved performance on both in-domain and out-of-domain data. The proposed approach is evaluated on several benchmark datasets, demonstrating its effectiveness in improving ASR accuracy and reducing language mismatch. The results suggest that self-supervised ASR using LID has great potential for developing more robust and accurate ASR systems in multilingual environments.

articleTitle: Estimation of Activation Sequences of Heart Using Cardiac Cell Models
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: One of the most common causes of death globally in the past few years is cardiac arrhythmia (irregular heartbeat), which occurs when the electric signals that coordinate the heartbeat don't work appropriately. As a result, there is a need to focus on understanding the basic mechanisms of heart rhythm variations. This paper focuses on cardiac excitation and uses a model replicating the electrical behavior of heart cells to generate an action potential. The activation times of the selected sources on the heart's surface from ECGSIM were compared with those generated using an electronic circuit model. The findings indicated a good match between the simulation results with a minimal error rate of milliseconds. The computational modeling of the electrical model of the cardiac cell was performed to explore the effect of the space or length constant (λ), which measures how well a potential spreads along the heart cell as a function of distance.

articleTitle: ATCNN-DWT Integration: A Combined Approach for Advanced Medical Image Fusion
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: The AdaptTransferCNN-DWT (ATCNN-DWT) Network offers an innovative approach to fusing multi-modal medical images. Traditionally, image fusion techniques from different modalities relied either on spatial or transform domain methods. Deep-learning CNN models, representing the spatial domain, sometimes result in blurred image boundaries and diminished texture detail. Addressing this limitation, our proposed hybrid model synergizes strengths from both domains. The process begins with AdaptTransferCNN (ATCNN) extracting salient features from source images. The fusion phase then incorporates the Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT), which integrates the ATCNN-generated image with another source image, enhancing subtle details. After undergoing Inverse DWT (IDWT), the resultant image successfully encapsulates the best from both domains. When benchmarked against five other fusion techniques, the ATCNN-DWT method demonstrated superior performance across multiple evaluation metrics.

articleTitle: A Modified Class Topper Algorithm and its Hybridization for Clustering Agriculture, Health-care and Geology Data
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: In this study, a modified class topper optimization algorithm named as MCTO is proposed for clustering problem. In the MCTO, cloning, crossover and mutation operators are introduced for global and faster convergence and better quality solutions. Two different types of hybridizations with K-means named as K-MCTO and MCTO-K are then performed with the MCTO to check the effectiveness. First, local optimal solutions obtained from the K-means is fed to the MCTO to get a global optimal solution. Then, another hybridization is done by feeding the solutions obtained from the MCTO to the K-means. Experimental study shows that the MCTO, K-MCTO and MCTO-K outperform various well-known state-of-the-arts. The algorithms are validated by clustering five standard data sets taken from agriculture, health-care and geology domains.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Intelligence Strategies for UAV-Assisted Device Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: In the rapidly evolving landscape of next-generation communication networks, such as 6G, addressing challenges related to on-demand connectivity in emergency scenarios has become a paramount concern. This study explores the domain of device communication within Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) networks, aiming to harness the potential of swarm intelligence techniques to improve the communication efficiency. This research centres on a comparative exploration of several well-established swarm intelligence approaches, including Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Cuckoo Search Optimization (CSO), and Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO). The primary objective is to assess the effectiveness and efficiency of these strategies in tackling the intricate challenges posed by on-demand connectivity in emergency situations within the UAV-assisted device communication network. The research aims to provide a deeper understanding of the comparative performance of the different approaches, guiding future decision-making processes.

articleTitle: A Photonic Crystal Fiber based SPR Biosensor for Escherichia Coli(E-Coli) Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: This article investigates a photonic crystal fiber(PCF) based surface plasmon resonance biosensor for the detection of the presence of E-coli bacteria in water. The presented sensing device is based on PCF designed with a hybrid lattice comprising one circular ring as the innermost one and two hexagonal rings surrounding it. A full-vectorial finite element method is used for modal analysis of the PCF design. The phase-matching condition occurs at 0.693µm,1.332µm, 1.78µm. The maximum wavelength sensitivity of 3472 nm/RIU, when the range of refractive index (RI)is from 1.401 to 1.585 and 2434 nm/RIU when the range of refractive index (RI) is from 1.585 to 1.769. The maximum amplitude sensitivity for our sensor is observed at -474.4629 RIU, and -474.4629737 RIU at 0.63µm and 1.777 µm respectively.

articleTitle: Graphene based Microwave Sensor for Determining Dielectric Permittivity of Different Materials for Food Evaluation Application
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: In this work single port graphene based planar microwave sensor is presented for characterizing dielectric permittivity of different materials. The proposed rectangular microstrip antenna sensor operated at 4.81 GHz having overall physical size 7 x 5 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> printed on flexible FR-4 substrate with relative permittivity (ϵr) = 4.4 and thickness 0.4mm, covering the bandwidth of 1562 MHz. The miniaturized antenna sensor investigates the relationship between dielectric permittivity and resonant frequency for different dielectric materials to employ proposed antenna sensor in food quality assessment effectively. Also, the proposed antenna-based sensor has potential to be utilized in various other industries such as agriculture, biomedical and pharmaceuticals for future endeavour.

articleTitle: Modeling and Simulation of Suspension for Electric Vehicle: Comfort vs. Road Holding Trade-offs
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: The paper deals with the modeling of the vehicle suspension, which consists of dampers, springs, and tires. The paper focuses on the dynamic analysis of vertical vibration of the suspension, which is described by a mathematical quarter car model. The suspension model is excited by stochastic road profiles. Spectral responses are obtained from the quarter car suspension model through the solution of differential equations. The objective of this paper is to evaluate conventional passive suspension in terms of ride comfort, which affects the passengers in the vehicle, and also in terms of road holding, which impacts safety. The article presents the relationship between comfort and road holding of the vehicle. This relationship assesses suspension from both perspectives and shows that increasing comfort and road holding simultaneously are conflicting objectives.

articleTitle: Enlightening University Students about Containerization through an Interactive Webpage
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Enlightenment about containerization is crucial for staying up-to-date with modern software development practices. It enables effective utilization of container orchestration platforms, efficient application deployment and management, enhanced portability and scalability, cost savings, and future technology adoption. However, the integration of containerization education in universities is often limited, highlighting the need for educational resources to bridge this knowledge gap. To address this gap, this work aims to create a web application dedicated to promoting awareness and providing educational resources on containerization.

articleTitle: Fractional Order PID Controller for Quadrotor
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: In recent years, research on Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) has intensified due to their versatile applications. While there are various forms of UAVs, each with its distinct properties and uses, controlling them remains a challenge. This paper focuses on the use of a quadcopter to control altitude via a fractional order PID (FOPID). Additionally, a genetic algorithm (GA) is employed to tune the parameters of the FOPID controller. The research incorporates a simulation, executed in Simulink/MATLAB, which illustrates the efficacy of the FOPID. A notable advantage of the fractional order PID is its enhanced response and superior adaptability, which culminates in improved, consistent performance.

articleTitle: Application of Gradient Boosting and Digital Simulation for Burner Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Machine learning algorithms are currently actively employed in the combustion field, streamlining the analysis of extensive combustion data derived from experiments or simulations across various space-time parameters. This facilitates the identification of latent patterns inherent in the data. Achieving optimal combustion processes involves stabilizing the flame and minimizing emissions of various harmful gases, including greenhouse gases. This study explores the application of a machine learning approach to classify the operational modes of a gas-oil burner by utilising experimental data obtained from a digital model within a Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) system. The machine learning techniques proposed in this investigation aim to advance technologies that ensure optimal operational conditions while mitigating the release of harmful substances. Specifically, a boosting model was selected and subsequently trained in this study.

articleTitle: ChatGPT and the Social Media Echo: A Sentiment Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: The breakthrough in Large Language Models and Artificial Intelligence brought about by OpenAI stirred up instinctive responses from the software ecosystem over social media platforms such as Twitter and Facebook. We hereby provide a comprehensive study on the Sentiments of public channeled onto Social Media towards the latest helm of Technology. We have aimed to encapsulate the dynamic interplay between human emotions and cutting-edge technology such as ChatGPT, providing a visualized context on user emotions and sentiments.

articleTitle: Development of Virtual Soil Moisture Sensor (VSMS) using Optical and Microwave Remote sensing data
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: In this research VSMS (Virtual Soil Moisture Sensor) is prepared by the help of Optical MODIS (Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectro-radiometer sensor and Microwave (MW) SAR (Synthetic Aperture Radar) sensor from Indian RISAT (Radar Imaging Satellite)-1. In reality VSMS is a pictorial (or map) format of soil information for an area of interest (AOI) at the level of 250 meter. For developing VSMS a linear regression equation drive from SM based on Optical data through Temperature Vegetation Dryness Index (TVDI) and SM based on MW data though Modified Water Cloud Model (MWCM). This VSMS is important because it have a good special resolution of 250 meter, precise value of SM during bad weather condition (this capability from MW data) and temporal resolution of par day (this capability from MODIS data).

articleTitle: Design of CMOS-Based Ring Oscillator for VCO Application Using Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: In recent years, the use of wireless transmission has increased tremendously. In these systems, voltage-controlled oscillators (VCO) are commonly used as clock generators for many applications. Ring oscillators is a major component of VCO which is manufactured using CMOS preferred to LC oscillators because of their reduced size and increased tuning range. The CMOS-based circuit design is complicated because of the non-linear relationship and lack of a mathematical model between the input parameters. Ring oscillators can be used as VCO by tuning the frequency values. In this, an MOS capacitance tunes the frequency by changing the capacitance and drain current through the inverter stages. It is impractical and hard to design such circuits through conventional methods. Therefore, this paper uses a neural networks-based model to design the circuit, and output is predicted. It is observed from the results that the output of the designed ring oscillator is approximately equal to the predicted values using the neural network.

articleTitle: Predicting Defective and Good Tyre Quality Status with Pre-Trained CNN Models
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Tyres are a critical organization for the safety, performance and driving comfort of vehicles. The qualities of tires are one of the direct characteristics of the travel experience and have a great impact on the safety of passengers and passengers. In recent years, thanks to developments in image processing and artificial intelligence technologies, the use of image-based methods in the color determination process of tires has increased significantly. Considering these conditions, tire errors were detected in two models to detect these extinguisher tire errors. Tire Classification Dataset was used to make these explanations. SqueezeNet and InceptionV3 pre-trained models were used as the classification model. As a result of the work done, a accuracy rate of 94.1% was achieved with the SqueezeNet model and 94.8% with the InceptionV3 model. It is envisaged that tire temperature, which can be integrated into the systems of the proposed models, can be detected quickly and reliably.

articleTitle: A Cluster Based Routing Protocol for IoT Based WSNs to Enhance Performance
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: In recent years, the most significant challenges in WSN – "Wireless sensor networks" are localization issues. Further, it is difficult to evaluate and monitored the data gathered with the beacons and localization method to evaluate node location. It is significant to develop an effective "Distance-Vector-Hop (DV-Hop)" algorithm in studies that focuses on better formulation to handle an average hop-size with the aid of a beacon in order to reduce error in localization with the measurement of distance between the dumb and beacon nodes because of improved localization accuracy. The current research utilizes the "WSN-based Internet of things Network Deployment" and an improvised routing protocol based on clustering for performance and security enhancement. The proposed routing protocol can be considered as "Cluster-Based Routing Protocol with Static Hub (CRPSH)" which discovers all possible paths prior to their use. The proposed method obtained lower localization-error than DV-Hop and localization algorithms (others) based on simulation results accuracy. Eventually, in the calculation of average end-to-end delay values on each type of procured results on Direct is 0.211061ms, LEACH is 0.165833ms Hop-by-hop is 0.160808ms, CORPL is 0.326439ms, and proposed method is 0.155783ms, which increases the performance and security.

articleTitle: Multirate VBR Model of Synchronous Machines for EMTP-Type Simulation Programs
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Models of electrical machines are essential in electromagnetic transient programs (EMTP) that are commonly used for studies of power systems. Recently, a voltage-behind-reactance (VBR) model has been developed for synchronous machines as an alternative to the conventional qd0 model which has advantageous properties in terms of interfacing and accuracy when using large simulation time steps. This paper presents a multirate implementation method for the VBR models of the synchronous machines in EMTP solution. The multirate algorithm separates the VBR machine model into fast subsystem (that includes the stator interfacing circuit and uses small time steps) and slow subsystem (that includes the rotor history terms and mechanical subsystem and uses larger time steps). The presented computer studies demonstrate the computational gains offered by the proposed multirate VBR model.

articleTitle: Capacitive Proximity Sensor Using Dickson Pump Charge Circuit
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Capacitive proximity sensing (CPS) has gained significant attention in modern electronic applications due to its non-contact nature and reliability in detecting nearby objects. This paper presents a comparative analysis of five distinct circuits with slight variations using NI MULTISIM, focusing on three key factors: gain performance, circuit complexity, and applicability for capacitive proximity sensing. The study evaluates the gain performance of the circuits, with the 6-diode Dickson charge pump circuit emerging as the clear winner, exhibiting an impressive gain. This circuit's exceptional sensitivity and broad detection range make it highly suitable for applications demanding precision and accurate sensing outcomes. In conclusion, this paper highlights the significance of selecting the most appropriate circuit for capacitive proximity sensing applications. Engineers and researchers may use this thorough study to make well-informed choices when constructing capacitive proximity sensors for a variety of applications.

articleTitle: High Voltage Circuit Breakers Arcing Contacts Operational Condition Indices Extracted from the Dynamic Resistance and Contact Motion Trajectory
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: The utmost importance of high voltage circuit breakers in the electrical power grid highlights the essential need for their reliability. To ensure this, accurate condition assessment methods for core components like the main contact system are crucial. Dynamic resistance measurement plays a key role as it assesses arcing contacts' condition without contact chamber disassembly. This paper endeavors to meticulously investigate and illuminate the pertinent indices derived from dynamic resistance measurements and motion trajectory waveforms, showcasing their efficacy through two real-world case studies conducted under varied testing scenarios. The analysis underscores the proposed indices' effectiveness, enhancing comprehension of the arcing contact assessment method.

articleTitle: Reducing Computation Requirements for Autonomous Mobile Robots on Low Powered Embedded Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Fully autonomous mobile robots have the potential to revolutionize various industries, from warehouse management to hospital logistics and last-mile deliveries. However, a significant obstacle to achieving reliable autonomy lies in the high computational and energy requirements. In response to this challenge, our paper introduces two innovative algorithms: the Pure Image Segmentation Approach (PISA) and the UNet Based Approach to Semantic Segmentation (UBASS). PISA leverages classical computer vision techniques, offering a fresh perspective on solving crucial tasks such as object detection, object avoidance, and lane detection. In contrast, UBASS harnesses the power of deep learning algorithms for semantic segmentation, unlocking new capabilities in robot perception. Our experiments showcase the effectiveness of these algorithms, demonstrating their accuracy and computational efficiency. Notably, PISA and UBASS outperform or match traditional techniques, including End-to-End Deep Learning and Canny Edge Detection, in terms of both task performance and resource utilization. This research contributes to the advancement of autonomous mobile robotics by offering practical and efficient solutions for navigation and perception challenges. By combining classic and contemporary approaches, we aim to inspire further research in the field, ultimately paving the way for more accessible and dependable autonomous mobile robots.

Author Keywords: UBASS. PISSA. Low Powered Embedded Systems

articleTitle: A Compact and Superstrate-Loaded Implantable Antenna for Leadless Cardiac Pacemaker System at ISM Band
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: The inclusion of Leadless Cardiac Pacemakers (LCP) into the world of pacemakers has led to the development of compact implantable antennas. In this communication, a compact and superstrate-loaded implantable antenna is designed for LCP systems in the Industrial, Scientific and Medical (ISM) band. The proposed antenna has a small footprint of 10 x 10 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and is designed on a 0.635 mm thick Rogers RO Duroid 3010 substrate and superstrate material with a relative permittivity (ɛr) of 10.2 and a loss tangent (δ) of 0.0022. To prevent contact between the tissue and metal radiator, same material is employed as a superstrate on both sides of antenna. The size of proposed antenna is greatly reduced by employing the slotting approach in patch and ground plane. The antenna is first developed using a multilayer tissue model and then it is validated using Hugo voxel model. The proposed antenna is distinguished by its miniaturized dimension, superstrate-loading, broad bandwidth, acceptable SAR and satisfactorygain values in comparison to other implantable antennas. The simulated impedance bandwidths of antenna are 17.76 % and 26.5 % while the maximum simulated gain of antenna is -25.24 dB and -15.93 dB in multilayer tissue model and Hugo voxel model. Moreover, the distributions of specific absorption rate (SAR) in both scenarios are also evaluated, making the designed antenna an appropriate choice for LCP systems.

articleTitle: EarSiamNet: Leveraging Siamese Networks and SVM for Ear Biometric Authentication
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Biometric breakthroughs have opened up new opportunities for personal identification and verification. We present a fresh methodology in this research study that focuses on using ear characteristics as a valid biometric for identification and verification. Our method involves extracting numerous features from ear samples and then feeding them into a one- shot classifier and a Support Vector Machine (SVM). These classifiers are taught to recognize and validate the provided candidate sample against a known sample. What makes our method fresh is the usage of a simple, lightweight model that is easily deployable on edge biometric devices without requiring a large number of samples. Our studies show that our proposed methodology is effective and has great potential. We obtain a high level of accuracy in recognizing and confirming the ear samples by using the one-shot classifier and SVM; The combination of our one-shot model and Histogram Of Oriented Gradient (HOG) feature extractor yielded an accuracy of 97.857%. The proposed method shows success in various identification and verification scenarios, including access control systems, forensics, and personalized healthcare.

articleTitle: ASIC Design and Implementation of a Power-Delay Product Optimized Arithmetic Operational Unit
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: The architectural design of a 16-bit arithmetic operational unit that has an optimized power-delay product is introduced using the technique of iterative carry-save addition and error-tolerant addition. The incorporation of Low-Power Selector Based Error-Tolerant Adders in the design and implementation of the iterative carry-save adder and multiplier enhances the speed and lowers the power consumption. The proposed arithmetic operational unit is modelled using Verilog hardware description language. The ASIC implementation and synthesis is performed using Cadence Genus tool with 45 and 90 nm gpdk standard technology libraries. A considerable reduction was noticed in the power, delay, and PDP of the proposed arithmetic operational unit.

articleTitle: Efficient Implementation of Fast Half Adder using 8T SRAM for In-Memory Computing Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: The recent development of data-intensive applications has resulted in crucial limitations in the conventional Von Neumann computing architecture. A highly significant advancement of in-memory computing has introduced an innovative approach to addressing this difficulty. This work presents a novel conceptualization of half-adder which is effectively incorporated into a memory array. The proposed design utilizes an 8T static random-access memory (SRAM) together with a multi-logic sense amplifier design. The architectural innovation outlined in the following description effectively utilizes the functions of three logic gates to carry out the essential activities of a half-adder. Significantly, this version of the half adder exhibits a significant reduction of 25% in time delay when compared to its existing designs which depended on a standard latch-type sense amplifier. The increased processing speed carries significant implications, particularly within the realm of managing contemporary data-intensive applications. Furthermore, this occurrence emphasizes the significant influence of memory-based computing within the domain of computing.

articleTitle: Monitoring and Control of Discrete-Event System Using Augmented Reality and Open-Source PLC
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: This paper deals with the interfacing of open-source PLC (Programmable Logic Controller) with augmented reality. The goal is to create an interactive environment for monitoring and control of automation processes. Creating new types of human-machine interfaces (HMIs) is one of the challenges of the Industry 4.0 concept and also relates to the Industry 5.0, which is the coming revolution to be human-centric. The practical part of the project focuses on the implementation of interfacing between PLC and augmented reality using OPC UA (Open Platform Communications Unified Architecture) and MQTT (MQ Telemetry Transport) interfaces. The work results in creation of working prototype that uses 3D engine Unity and ARCore library to create an interactive augmented reality environment.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of UAV Assisted Dual-Hop Multi-user Uplink NOMA System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: In this paper we have presented an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-assisted non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) based communication model where UAV is working as a data collection unit (CU) for different IoT sensor nodes (ISN). In the proposed uplink model IoT-CU link is characterized by Rayleigh channel and mm-wave link between CU to BS is characterized by κ−µ channel. Multiple ISNs are being serviced by using NOMA scheme. The closed form expression for outage probability of each user has been presented. Further we have verified the mathematical frame-work with Monte-Carlo simulations. Simulation results shows the close agreement with analytical results.

articleTitle: Water Quality Analysis Using Normalized Difference Chlorophyll Index (NDCI) and Normalized Difference Turbidity Index (NDTI), Using Google Earth Engine Platform
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: The study investigates seasonal variations in chlorophyll content and water quality, emphasizing their impact on vegetation growth and ecosystem health, with a focus on the pre-monsoon, monsoon, and post-monsoon seasons. Over a five-year period, the pre-monsoon emerges as critical for vegetation vitality, marked by higher chlorophyll levels due to favorable conditions like optimal temperature, moisture, and nutrients. The northern region stands out as a hotspot for elevated pre-monsoon chlorophyll content. During the monsoon and post-monsoon seasons, chlorophyll content fluctuates due to erratic rainfall, variable cloud cover, and temperature changes, disrupting sustained photosynthesis. Water quality, assessed using NDTI, reveals elevated turbidity in pre-monsoon months, contrasting with clearer waters during the monsoon and post-monsoon periods. This is attributed to factors like sedimentation, nutrient runoff, and human activities, with the northern region consistently experiencing higher turbidity levels during pre-monsoon periods, indicating localized influences needing further investigation.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Models for Energy Consumption Prediction in Residential Buildings
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: The prediction of energy consumption in residential buildings has emerged as a crucial area of study in recent times, owing to the substantial demand for energy-efficient solutions. In this paper, a comparative analysis of diverse machine learning models is presented, encompassing Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), Artificial Neural Networks (ANN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Random Forest, Linear Regression, Autoencoder, Hybrid (Random Forest-MLP), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Ensemble, and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), for predicting energy consumption in residential buildings. The performance of each model is evaluated using Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) and Mean Absolute Error (MAE) values. The outcomes demonstrate that Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) outperforms all other models in terms of both RMSE and MAE values, making it a promising solution for predicting energy consumption in residential buildings.

articleTitle: Enhancing Wastewater Treatment Plant Efficiency: Constraint Optimization and Regression Analysis Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: This research work presents a comprehensive approach to optimizing wastewater treatment processes, emphasizing the improvement of both the energy efficacy of aeration and effluent quality. A multi-step methodology that combines the Genetic Algorithm (GA) optimization technique, data collection, linear regression analysis, constraint formulation, and the application of constrained optimization was adopted. In the initial phase, unconstrained GA optimization was used to find the values of the decision variables that optimized the objectives: aeration energy and effluent quality index. The dataset acquired during this phase indicated the values of the decision variables, objective functions, and other important variables such as effluent ammonia and nitrogen concentration. Linear regression analysis was performed using this dataset to establish linear correlations between the decision variables and the constraint variables. Constraint equations were then formulated using the coefficient values. A new GA optimization was executed with added constraints. The optimal values for the decision variables, which adhered to the constraints, were identified. The methodology presented here provides a robust, data-driven framework for optimizing wastewater treatment processes, with the potential for substantial energy savings and improved environmental performance in water treatment facilities.

articleTitle: Comparison of Various Meteorological Parameters for Solar Radiation Prediction Using Artificial Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Renewable energy sources are currently considered an alternative source of energy because they swiftly regenerate themselves and may be utilized repeatedly. Weather, time of day, and geographic location all affect solar radiation. In the proposed work, solar radiation is predicted using an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) model. The prediction of diffuse insolation under a clear sky is done using the neural fitting tool (nftool). The suggested ANN model's mean square error and regression values are generated using the various meteorological data, such as humidity, air temperature, atmospheric pressure, and the number of days in the year, as input. The performance of the forecast solar radiation is then assessed using the various combinations of meteorological factors produced and applied to the neural network.

articleTitle: Improving Diabetic Retinopathy Diagnosis with Transfer Learning and Filtered Fundus Images: An Automated Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a critical eye disease affecting individuals with diabetes, leading to potential vision loss if not diagnosed and treated promptly. In this study, we proposed an automated system for the detection of diabetic retinopathy. This system incorporates a preprocessing stage, wherein a 3D image is constructed from the optimal output of a selection of three filters. Subsequently, a model is trained through transfer learning, enabling it to extract pertinent features. Classification is performed through the utilization of a fully connected layer. Experimental results on the Messidor dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methodology. EfficientNet achieves the highest accuracy of 95% among the explored deep models, highlighting its potential for accurate diabetic retinopathy detection.

articleTitle: Hexagon Shaped Six Port DRA based MIMO Antenna with Pattern Diversity for Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: The presented antenna contains six cylindrical dielectric resonators which are mounted on six rectangular substrates arranged in a hexagonal fashion and are placed on six edges of a hexagonal-shaped FR-4 substrate. The hexagonal substrate serves as a common ground for each of the six rectangular substrates. Feeding of this antenna is given by using a ring aperture in the rectangular ground plane. This antenna radiates in six directions such that any two consecutive radiation peaks are separated by 60° in the azimuthal plane. This unique feature allows this antenna to be used for six-direction transmission or reception. The antenna has the maximum dimensions of 59.4 × 66. 6 × 28.0 mm and the operating frequency range of 4.96 - 5.62 GHz with a resonance frequency of 5.2 GHz. The isolation between the ports is more than 19 dB for the overall operating frequency range. The MIMO parameters are within the legitimate limits. This antenna can be used for WLAN (5.15-5.35 GHz) and WiMAX (5.5 GHz) applications.

articleTitle: Design and Numerical Investigation of FTO/TiO2/FA0.85Cs0.15Pb(I0.85Br0.15)3/MoO3/Au Perovskite Solar Cell
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: The primary aim of the present work is to design a perovskite photovoltaic cell with higher efficacy that is suitable for practical applications. Therefore, a mixed perovskite layer composed of FA<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.85</inf>Cs<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.15</inf>Pb(I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.85</inf>Br<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.15</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> was used as the active layer. Along with this perovskite, TiO2 and MoO3 have been used as electron and hole transport layer, respectively. The cell was optimized by varying the working temperature between 280K to 325K, absorber layer thickness between 100nm to 700nm, and bulk defect density between 1011/Cm-3 to 1016/Cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup>. The final Optimized cell shows 1.53V open circuit voltage, 23.67mA/Cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> short circuit current, 85.63% of fill factor and 30.84% of efficiency at optimized temperature of 280K, optimized perovskite layer thickness of 700nm and bulk defect density of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sup> Cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The present modeling technique is compared with the reported theoretical as well as experimental data that confirm the accuracy of the conclusions we have obtained for the proposed cell.

articleTitle: Project Lingua Franca: Democratizing Information through Unified Optical Character Recognition and Neural Machine Translation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Document Translations are considered to be an unsolved problem with respect to dependable translations across languages. This process is time-consuming in nature and requires human intervention, primarily due to the inability of current methods to develop an understanding of the local context within the document. This is also a problem from the lens of accessibility, as a large section of the human population does not know English. In our work, we demonstrate how our proposed method, termed Project Lingua Franca, has the ability to generate document translations in a cheap and fairly efficient method, with no prior training and in Zero-shot settings.

articleTitle: Develop Soil Moisture Data Using Optical and Microwave Satellite Observations
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: High spatial (250 m) and temporal (daily) resolution Soil Moisture (SM) data was generated by developing a linear regrration (LR) relationship (R2= 0.95) between 250 m SM derived from TVDI (based on Optical and Thermal data) and MWCM (based on Microwave data). On the basis of statistical tests, we found that developed SM data is in good agreement with in-situ observations. Therefore, daily SM data at 250 m spatial resolution can be generated for agricultural applications like monitoring and assessment of agricultural drought.

articleTitle: Enhancing Microarchitecture Performance through Synergistic Dynamic Branch Prediction and Cache Prefetching
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: In the dynamic landscape of modern microarchitecture design, performance optimization remains a perpetual pursuit. As deeply pipelined microarchitectures navigate the challenges posed by conditional branches, and memory access latency continues to cast its shadow, a holistic approach that harnesses the synergistic potential of dynamic branch prediction and cache prefetching emerges as a promising avenue. This paper delves into the intricacies of these two techniques, their individual significance, and their transformative impact when combined and accordingly proposed two novel techniches: HiPred and Confidence based Stream Prefetcher. The HiPred dynamic branch predictor introduces a hierarchical scheme that transcends accuracy thresholds, while the Confidence based Stream Prefetcher (CSP) strategically anticipates memory needs. The HiPred dynamic branch predictor innovatively employs a hierarchical structure that harnesses the predictive strengths of two distinct predictors whereas CSP meticulously localizes miss/access address streams and proactively orchestrates the caching of frequently accessed data. Experimental evaluation of these two techniques depicts that HiPred yields a remarkable accuracy rate exceeding 98% where as CSP orchestrates a performance uplift ranging from 10% to 20% across seven distinct SPEC benchmarks.

articleTitle: Clinical Efficacy Of Ensemble Learning For Cardiovascular Disease Prediction: A Comparative Analysis With Traditional Machine Learning Classifiers
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Cardiovascular diseases pose a substantial global health burden. Therefore, it is crucial to have a timely and accurate prediction of such diseases for an effective healthcare intervention. This research comprehensively analyze the effectiveness of classical machine learning and ensemble learning techniques in predicting heart disease. On a diverse dataset with clinical, demographic, and lifestyle factors, the performance of these models is empirically assessed using a variety of performance metrics, such as cross-validation mean accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, and ROC - AUC Score. Through this comprehensive analysis, this research concludes that ensemble learning techniques outperform conventional machine learning classifiers in terms of accuracy and robustness. Gradient Boost has the best overall cross-validation accuracy score of 88.69% and recall of 89.71%. In summary, this study aims to enhance cardiovascular disease management and reducing associated mortality rates.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Full Adder and Full Subtractor Circuit Using Hybrid Logic Style
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Minimization delay and low-power consumable logic devices are the significant challenges in designing a digital microelectronic circuit. Most electronic gadgets comprise arithmetic logic units (ALU), a significant part of the processor. The processors are consuming high power and causing more delay due to the low performance of arithmetic logic units. The performance of the electronic circuit is enhanced by increasing the performance of the ALU. The essential component of an ALU is an adder circuit. The adder circuit is used for addition and other arithmetic operations such as multiplication, division, and address calculation. In this article, the design and analysis of full adder and full subtractor circuits are carried out. It is designed using the XOR-XNOR logic circuit, which consumes less power and minimizes delay. The performance of these circuits is dependent on the XOR-XNOR logic module. The difference and borrow circuits are designed using CMOS logic and transmission gate logic. An XOR-XNOR circuit can reduce delay and power and get full swing (FS) output. The hybrid logic style based full adder and subtractor parameters like power, delay, noise margin, and the number of transistors.

articleTitle: Autoencoders in Graphical Document Retrieval: Cost Function Influence and Rotation Impact
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: This study explores autoencoder application in graphical document retrieval, focusing on rotation’s impact. Specific to this paper are scanned floor plan images. We investigate the pivotal role of cost functions—specifically, Mean Squared Error (MSE) and Consistency Loss—in shaping autoencoder behavior and retrieval accuracy. By subjecting autoencoders to the challenges posed by rotated graphical documents, we decipher the extent to which rotation impacts retrieval outcomes. Concurrently, we dissect the nuanced influence of distinct cost functions on retrieval accuracy, shedding light on their diver-gent contributions. Through rigorous experimentation, we show autoencoder adaptability to rotation and cost function effects on retrieval precision. Our findings underline the significance of cost function selection in enhancing retrieval accuracy. Our insights hold implications for optimizing, refining autoencoder-based methods, empowering digital document analysis practitioners.

articleTitle: Unveiling Customer Segmentation Patterns in Credit Card Data using K-Means Clustering: A Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Customer segmentation plays a crucial role in business development by providing deep insights into customer behaviors and preferences, facilitating effective and personalized marketing strategies. However, traditional segmentation methods often fall short of accurately analyzing large and complex datasets. In recent years, the application of machine learning techniques has transformed the field of customer segmentation, enabling automated analysis, enhanced accuracy, and the discovery of intricate patterns and key trends. This research paper provides a detailed review of the application of K-Means clustering in credit card companies for effective customer segmentation. It explores the benefits, challenges, and practical considerations of utilizing K-Means clustering, along with real-world case studies highlighting trends and potential advancements for using K-Means clustering in credit card customer segmentation.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Subsea Pipeline Defect Classification Using Supervised Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Modeling, Simulation & Intelligent Computing (MoSICom)
abstract: Subsea pipelines are pivotal to a country’s economy. These pipelines not only ensure safe and efficient transportation of gas, oil, and other refined products but also enable continuous flow of oil and gas to onshore reserves, thereby maintaining a consistent supply to meet energy demands.
